mainEntity.name: Do you provide rehabilitation clinic cleaning in Stoughton, MA?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Stoughton (Norfolk County) is one of the 109 Massachusetts cities and towns we serve. It is about 28 miles southeast of our Marlborough base in a straight line. Every engagement starts with a free on-site assessment; call (978) 307-8107.

mainEntity.name: Who is the local health authority in Stoughton?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Stoughton Board of Health; its official page is https://www.stoughton.org/447/Health. Clinics, hospitals and long-term care facilities are licensed and surveyed by the Massachusetts Department of Public Health, while the local board of health handles local environmental-health matters under the State Sanitary Code and local regulations. mainEntity.name: Our therapists wipe the tables and mats between patients. Is that enough?

acceptedAnswer.text: Wiping is cleaning, and cleaning is not disinfection. They are two steps. Treatment tables, mats, weights, and bands that contact intact skin are non-critical items that need to be cleaned and then disinfected between patients at the level the degree of soiling requires, per the CDC Infection Prevention Checklist non-critical item definition and CDC Core Practices 5f. Between-patient turnover stays with your clinicians, because they are the ones in the room. What we own is the end-of-day terminal pass across every table, mat, and plinth, plus floors, restrooms, and shared areas.

mainEntity.name: Our wipes dry in about twenty seconds. Does that still count as disinfection?

acceptedAnswer.text: Usually not. Nearly every disinfectant label carries a contact time during which the surface must remain visibly wet, and a surface that dries early was cleaned rather than disinfected. This is a documented finding pattern in outpatient settings under Section II item B of the CDC Infection Prevention Checklist and Core Practices 5b, alongside products used past shelf life or stored badly. On a warm vinyl mat, a single wipe rarely holds a two or four minute dwell. We match the product to the surface, reapply where needed, and train to the label.

mainEntity.name: Skin-to-equipment contact all day is our real exposure. What do you actually do about it?

acceptedAnswer.text: We treat the gym as a contact-transfer environment rather than an office. Every surface a patient's bare skin meets, including plinth vinyl, mat surfaces, exercise ball skins, bench pads, and the floor of the mat area, is cleaned and then disinfected on a defined interval with an EPA-registered product chosen for that surface. The mat floor gets a wet process rather than a dry mop that redistributes skin debris. Written policies naming the gym, the treatment tables, and the shared equipment are precisely what Section I item A of the CDC Infection Prevention Checklist asks a clinic to hold.

Citations Stoughton rehabilitation clinics can avoid

Real, published regulatory findings — every citation links to its source.

CDC Infection Prevention Checklist for Outpatient Settings, Section II item A; CDC Core Practices 5f

Shared equipment reprocessed in a way the manufacturer never specified. CDC's position is that where no cleaning and disinfection instructions exist, the item is not suitable for multi-patient use.

CDC Core Infection Prevention and Control Practices 5b; CDC Infection Prevention Checklist, Section II item A

High-touch surfaces close to the patient — plinth rails, parallel bars, equipment grips — not cleaned and disinfected on a more frequent schedule than other surfaces.

CDC Infection Prevention Checklist for Outpatient Settings, Section II item B; CDC Core Practices 5b

Disinfectant wipes used with insufficient contact time — the surface dries before the label kill time, or the product is past shelf life or badly stored.

Inside a Stoughton service visit

High-touch surfaces on every visit

  • Treatment tables and plinths
  • Exercise mats
  • Free weights, dumbbells and kettlebells
  • Resistance bands and handles
  • Door handles
  • Light switches

Our sequence, step by step

  1. Clean and disinfect treatment tables and mats with products compatible with vinyl and upholstery.
  2. Launder or replace reusable linens per the clinic's process — we do not take clinic linens off site unless contracted.
  3. Empty trash; sharps are rare but stay with the clinic's hauler if present.
  4. Damp-mop gym floors and vacuum carpeted areas.
  5. Log areas completed and any damaged equipment surfaces we notice.

A starting schedule

  • Treatment tables and shared equipment: between patients by staff, full clean daily.
  • Gym floor: daily.
  • Periodic: equipment deep clean and high dusting.

Rehabilitation clinics are typically cleaned after the last appointment, since the gym is in use all day.

Documentation you receive

  • Gym and treatment-room checklist
  • Safety Data Sheets
  • Signed service logs
  • Certificate of insurance

Questions worth asking at the walkthrough

  • Which products will you use on our table upholstery and mats?
  • What will our staff still need to wipe between patients?
  • What logs will we receive?

We answer each of these in writing after the free assessment.
